editorial_candidates.claim: The six finite-dimensional spaces V1=ker T, V2=ker(UT), V3=ker U, V4=coker T, V5=coker(UT), V6=coker U form the exact sequence 0→V1→V2→V3→V4→V5→V6→0; alternating dimensions cancel to yield ind(UT)=ind T+ind U.
editorial_candidates.maps_and_relations: Draw the objects V1,...,V6 in order and arrows α, β, γ, δ, ε as defined on line 48, with zero objects at the ends. Mark exactness at each Vi as proved in lines 52 and 54. The arrow labels must retain their source and target: α(x)=x, β(x)=Tx, γ(y)=y+ran T, δ(y+ran T)=Uy+ran(UT), ε(z+ran(UT))=z+ran U.
editorial_candidates.checks: Check each arrow source/target and preserve the quotient-coset domains of δ and ε. The intended use is to visualize exactness and the alternating-dimension cancellation; the proof itself already states and verifies these relations.
editorial_candidates.reason: The proof introduces six spaces and five maps, then verifies exactness in two long steps before telescoping dimensions. A linear exact-sequence schematic could make those map domains and the cancellation easier to scan, without adding a premise or proof content.
